thread.title: Should Spotify Join FANG Group Of Big Internet Stocks?

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Should Spotify Join FANG Group Of Big Internet Stocks?
text:
A Wall Street analyst who initiated coverage of Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) on Tuesday suggested in passing that the streaming music leader be included in the FANG group of top internet stocks.
X The FANG group includes Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ). Some analysts like to include Apple ( AAPL ) in the bunch for a FANG Plus or FAANG group.
Pivotal Research Group analyst Jeffrey Wlodarczak started coverage of Spotify with a buy rating and a price target of 200. Shares of the Swedish company lost 1.3% to close at 154.62 on the stock market today .
FAANGS? In a report titled "FAANGS?" he compared Spotify's business and leadership position to those of Netflix. Both offer subscription-based services in an underpenetrated market. Each made large investments in technology to create best-in-class offerings that work on any device. One big difference is Netflix's ability to create original content for its service, Wlodarczak said.

Please contact customer service CLOSE "In our view, Spotify is similar to such internet products as Netflix, Google search and Facebook (in) that once consumers try the service the experience is transformational and drives accelerating usage," he said.
Spotify is in a "two-horse" race with Apple in the premium streaming music space, Wlodarczak said. The market has "plenty of room" for other competitors including Amazon and Google, he said.
Spotify is the global leader in premium music streaming, a market that is "only in the third inning of a very healthy growth trajectory," he said. Consumers are in the early stages of shifting to subscription streaming and its "all-you-can-eat model for music consumption," he said.
Netflix Gets Price-Target Hike Elsewhere on the market Tuesday, MKM Partners raised its price target on Netflix to 390 from 320. The firm maintained its buy rating on the internet television network. However, analyst Rob Sanderson said Netflix is no longer a "top pick" given its massive increase in valuation recently, MarketWatch reported .
Netflix stock slipped 0.4% to close at 349.73. It hit a record high of 356.10 in intraday trading.
